question: Can practice in breath, intellect, or body still be valid from the nondual standpoint?
premises: In our view, breath, intellect, body, and the rest clearly share the nature of the all.
Because they are all-natured, practice situated in them is not excluded.
Such practice removes fixation on what is taken as other.
inference: From the nondual standpoint, practice in any of these supports can serve the removal of otherness because all are expressions of the same reality.
uncertainties: The sandhi-packed final compound allows slight variation in how tightly the causal and result clauses are joined.
plain_english: Or, in our view, breath, intellect, body, and the rest are clearly of the nature of the all. Because of that, even practice carried out in them removes the sense of otherness.
